ops.title: Swift .request frame omits the tenant-empty clause its ten siblings enforce
ops.description:
Found by the Lane B closing refuter, defect 4. Not exploitable today; the contract is asymmetric.

Sources/DaemonKit/SessionTransport.swift:477 — .request is the only kind of eleven whose
validation omits the frame.tenant.isEmpty clause. .stream at :503 has it. SessionFrame.tenant
(:171) is a public settable var.

Why it is not exploitable now: the Swift half is client-only (no request decode site), and a Go
daemon refuses the frame — the Go side proves 22/22 refusals across 11 kinds in both directions,
with an 11-row baseline showing each frame is valid without the tenant, so that table cannot pass
vacuously.

Why it still matters: D6 reserved Tenant as a must-be-empty header field, and the CHANGELOG
asserted "the codec per-kind contract refuses a request or stream frame carrying one, in both
directions" unqualified. That claim has been scoped to Go rather than made true. If Swift ever
grows a request decode site the asymmetry becomes live.

Sibling of the Swift Authorize gap (cc-notes 205ba99): both are places where the Swift mirror
is behind the Go half on a trust-adjacent contract.

ops.text: SessionTransport.swift .request validation carries the tenant-empty clause, matching its ten siblings
CHANGELOG can state the per-kind tenant contract without a Go-only qualifier
